item.research_question: How can a precipitation-strengthening strategy be used to design a high-entropy/medium-entropy alloy that sustains ultrahigh strength and excellent ductility simultaneously across a wide temperature range from cryogenic to elevated temperatures?
item.material_system: Al5(CoNiV)95 (at %) alloy, a CoNiV-based face-centered cubic (fcc)/B2 duplex medium-entropy alloy (MEA) with 5 at% Al added to an equiatomic fcc-structured CoNiV matrix; also Al7(CoNiV)93 for comparison
item.processing_route: Arc-melting high-purity (>99.9 at%) Al, Co, Ni, and V metals followed by suction-casting into a Cu mold; homogenization at 1373 K for 8 hours with water quenching; cold rolling with 65% thickness reduction; annealing at 1173 K for 1 hour with water quenching
item.test_conditions: Uniaxial tensile tests at 77 K, 298 K, 723 K, and 1073 K using a universal testing machine at a fixed strain rate of 10⁻³ s⁻¹; microstructural analysis via XRD, EBSD, TEM, and synchrotron high-energy XRD on tensile-fractured samples
key_findings: At room temperature (298 K), the alloy exhibited a yield strength of 1.1 GPa, ultimate tensile strength of 1.5 GPa, and tensile elongation of ~34%.
At cryogenic temperature (77 K), yield strength increased to 1.4 GPa, ultimate tensile strength to 1.9 GPa, with fracture elongation of ~38%.
At intermediate temperature (723 K), the alloy maintained a yield strength of 1.1 GPa with serrated stress-strain response and high strain hardening rates.
At high temperature (1073 K), the alloy showed enhanced ductility of ~74% and ultimate tensile strength of 0.28 GPa, attributed to dynamic recrystallization.
The alloy achieved the highest specific yield strength among reported ductile HEAs at ~150.2 MPa·cm³/g.
The volume fraction of the B2 phase in Al5(CoNiV)95 was estimated at ~6%, with B2 grain sizes ranging from several hundred nanometers to ~1 μm.
In the Al7(CoNiV)93 variant, increasing Al content raised the B2 phase volume fraction to ~21% and resulted in ~280% superplastic elongation at 1073 K.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the strength-ductility synergy to multiple deformation mechanisms: precipitation strengthening from Al-rich B2 nanoparticles; dynamic Hall-Petch effect where twin boundaries reduce dislocation mean free path; twinning-induced plasticity (TWIP) triggered by low stacking fault energy (SFE) in the fcc matrix; dynamic strain aging (DSA) at 723 K causing flow serrations; and dynamic recrystallization (DRX) enabling superplasticity at 1073 K. The B2 precipitates constrain the soft fcc matrix, generating back stresses, while twins mitigate interfacial stress concentrations to delay fracture.
item.limitations: The authors note that the Al7(CoNiV)93 variant exhibited a ductile-brittle transition when lowering temperature from 298 to 77 K due to increased B2 precipitate density. Additionally, the superplastic elongation of the Al5(CoNiV)95 alloy (~74%) was insufficient compared to other microduplex alloys, attributed to deformation-enhanced grain growth which could be mitigated by using high strain rates.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that high strain rates could be used to overcome deformation-enhanced grain growth and improve superplastic elongation. They also propose that the design strategy can be adapted by adjusting Al content to optimize the balance between strength and ductility, and that combining chemical complexity with conventional strengthening principles can justify the industrial costs of M/HEAs.
quotes: The ability of the alloy presented here to sustain this excellent strength-ductility synergy over a wide temperature range is aided by multiple deformation mechanisms i.e., twins, stacking faults, dynamic strain aging, and dynamic recrystallization.
The highest specific yield strength (~150.2 MPa·cm3/g) among reported ductile HEAs is obtained.

The appearance of twins close to B2 precipitates here plays a crucial role in offsetting this problem, via the mitigation and accommodation of high fcc-B2 interfacial stresses to prolong strain hardening due to limited plasticity of B2 precipitates.
